subject: Urban Planning
title: Vienna's Ringstraße: Boulevard of Power
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Vienna's Ringstraße: Boulevard of Power.

hook.text: In 1857, Emperor Franz Joseph tore down Vienna's walls and replaced them with the grandest boulevard ever.

buildup.text: The Ringstraße circled the old city with opera houses, museums, parliament, and a university — all new.

discovery.text: Each building used a different historical style: Greek for parliament, Gothic for city hall, Renaissance for university.

twist.text: Critics said the mismatched styles were theatrical fakery — a stage set masquerading as a city.

climax.text: Hitler studied the Ringstraße obsessively. His unrealized plans for Berlin directly copied it.

punchline.text: A boulevard of borrowed styles. Every dictator wanted one.

quiz.question: What replaced Vienna's medieval defensive walls?
options: A canal system inspired by Amsterdam
A grand circular boulevard lined with monumental buildings
A railway line connecting Vienna to Budapest
